messages:
erin: Quick one - our Kotlin SDK sample is hitting a 401 retry loop when the OkHttp Authenticator and a coroutine retry wrapper interact. Suspect interceptor/authenticator ordering or retry semantics. Anyone seen this?

daniel: Can you paste the high-level flow? Is this the Authenticator doing synchronous refresh + returning a new request? And you have a coroutine-based retry that replays the suspend call?

erin: Yup. Authenticator refreshes token synchronously (blocking) and returns a new Request with updated header. Our higher-level code wraps suspend calls in a retry loop that re-invokes the suspend call on network errors/401. Example:
```kotlin
suspend fun <T> withRetry(block: suspend ()->T): T {
  repeat(3) { try { return block() } catch(e: HttpException) { if(e.code()==401) continue } }
  throw RuntimeException("auth fail")
}
```
When the authenticator runs and refreshes, sometimes the retry wrapper triggers another parallel refresh (race) and we end up with duplicated refreshes and occasional 401 loops.

daniel: Are you using an OkHttp Authenticator (called from network interceptor path) or an Interceptor that does async refresh? Authenticator is retried by OkHttp itself and can be called multiple times on concurrent requests.

erin: It's an Authenticator implementation that synchronously calls token refresh endpoint using the same OkHttp client. We saw a deadlock once, so we use a separate client for refresh. Still, multiple concurrent refreshes happen and the retry wrapper sees 401s and retries, leading to thundering refreshes and occasional stale-token races.

daniel: Two things: 1) prefer to make the Authenticator idempotent with coordination (e.g., singleflight/mutex around refresh) and 2) have the higher-level retry not retry on 401 if the Authenticator will transparently retry. Otherwise both layers race.

hao: Also be careful with interceptor vs authenticator ordering. If you have a network interceptor that mutates Authorization header after Authenticator runs, you can end up reusing a request without refreshed creds.

erin: Good point. Our fix so far: add a refresh mutex around the refresh logic in the Authenticator (double-checked token read) and have the coroutine retry treat 401 as non-retriable (fail fast) since the client should have handled it. That removed the loop.

daniel: For SDK docs I suggest a short section: "Auth retry guidelines": prefer Authenticator-level refresh + singleflight coordination; avoid higher-level automatic 401 retries unless you implement coordination; if you must retry at app level, ensure you detect and wait for in-progress refreshes. Include code snippet showing a simple Mutex + token cache pattern.

build-bot: CI flaky detected: integration-tests/android-emu  symptom: repeated token refresh spikes. Ticket created INT-6023. Logs: https://ci.internal/12012

erin: I'll open a PR updating the Kotlin sample app and onboarding notes with the mutex pattern and a warning about app-level 401 retries. Will attach a minimal repro gist to INT-6023. Thanks!
